screen2-a1.glyph: dimmed grey strip along the right screen edge, no symbol of its own
screen2-a1.description: dimmed grey strip along the right edge beside the open side panel; the ghost glyph of the screen beneath shows through it
screen2-a1.visible_text: none; the only mark inside it is the dimmed ghost glyph belonging to the covered screen
screen2-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Close navigation menu" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen2-a1.convention_relied_on: tapping the dimmed area outside a side panel to close it is an Android convention, but the strip shows another control's glyph as its only face — my reading, confidence medium
screen2-a1.initial_rationale: the strip has no face of its own; what a user sees inside it is the ghost glyph, which suggests the strip does that glyph's job

test_cases.precondition: side panel open over the home screen
test_cases.action: tap exactly on the dimmed ghost glyph inside the strip
test_cases.expected_result: if the visible glyph conveyed the purpose, tapping it would do the ghost's job
test_cases.confirms_if: the tap does something other than what the visible glyph belongs to
test_cases.overturns_if: the tap does the ghost glyph's job, or the strip carries its own visible close cue
test_cases.observed_result: the side panel closed and nothing else happened; the screen stayed in normal (non-incognito) mode, so the glyph the user aimed at did not act

screen2-a1.deciding_evidence: the only visible thing in the strip is a glyph from the covered screen, and tapping it closes the panel instead of doing that glyph's job
screen2-a1.recommendation: dim the covered screen enough that its controls do not read as live, or give the panel its own visible close control (an X or 'Close') at the top

screen2-a2.description: large word 'Claude' at the top of the side panel
screen2-a2.visible_text: "Claude" (the product's name, set as a title)
screen2-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Claude" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen2-a2.initial_rationale: the visible text is the product's name; it reads as a title, not an action, and says nothing about what pressing it does

test_cases.expected_result: if the word conveyed a purpose, the result would be predictable from it
test_cases.confirms_if: something happens that the word does not predict
test_cases.overturns_if: nothing happens (then it is only a title) or the result is predictable from 'Claude'
test_cases.observed_result: the panel closed and an empty new chat opened with the keyboard up — a 'home / new chat' action the title word did not predict

screen2-a2.deciding_evidence: the title is actionable and starts a new chat, which the product name gives no hint of
screen2-a2.recommendation: make the title non-interactive, or label the action it performs (e.g. 'Home' / 'New chat')

screen2-a3.description: 'Chats' row with a speech-bubbles glyph in the side panel
screen2-a3.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Chats" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen2-a3.initial_rationale: plain word naming a destination: the list of your chats

test_cases.confirms_if: something other than a chats list opens
test_cases.observed_result: a screen titled 'Chats' opened with a search box and the list of past chats

screen2-a3.deciding_evidence: opened the Chats list it names

screen2-a4.description: 'Projects' row with a stacked-tray glyph in the side panel
screen2-a4.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Projects" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict

test_cases.observed_result: a 'Projects' screen opened with 'Create a project to organize chats with Claude around a topic or set of documents.'

screen2-a4.deciding_evidence: opened the Projects screen, which also explains what a project is

screen2-a5.description: 'Code' row with a </> glyph in the side panel
screen2-a5.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Code" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen2-a5.initial_rationale: 'Code' alone does not say whether this writes code, shows code, or opens a coding tool; a first-time user cannot tell what they get

test_cases.expected_result: if the word conveyed the purpose, the destination would be predictable
test_cases.confirms_if: the destination is something 'Code' did not predict
test_cases.overturns_if: a clearly code-related tool the user could have predicted opens
test_cases.observed_result: a page opened showing a sample coding conversation and the heading 'Upgrade for Claude Code' with 'Upgrade' and 'Return to chat' buttons — an upgrade offer for a separate product

screen2-a5.deciding_evidence: the row leads to a paid-product upgrade page; neither the product nor the paywall is conveyed by the single word 'Code'
screen2-a5.recommendation: name the destination, e.g. 'Claude Code (coding assistant) — Pro'

screen2-a6.description: 'Artifacts' row with a shapes glyph in the side panel
screen2-a6.accessibility_text_consulted: talkback_label "Artifacts" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen2-a6.initial_rationale: 'Artifacts' is product jargon; a first-time user does not know what an artifact is

test_cases.expected_result: if the word conveyed the purpose, the destination would explain itself
test_cases.confirms_if: the destination still does not say what an artifact is
test_cases.overturns_if: the destination defines artifacts in plain words
test_cases.observed_result: an 'Artifacts' screen opened with the empty-state line 'Artifacts you've had with Claude will show up here.' — circular; it never says what an artifact is

screen2-a6.deciding_evidence: neither the row nor the screen it opens explains the term
screen2-a6.recommendation: rename or caption it in plain words, e.g. 'Artifacts — documents, code and designs Claude made for you'

screen2-a7.glyph: orange filled circle containing the letters AC
screen2-a7.description: orange circle with the letters 'AC' at the bottom-left of the side panel
screen2-a7.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Ally Cooper, Settings" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen2-a7.convention_relied_on: a circle with the user's initials is an established account/profile avatar convention leading to account settings — my reading, confidence medium
screen2-a7.initial_rationale: initials avatar convention for 'your account'; exemption pending the behavioural test

test_cases.observed_result: a 'Settings' screen opened with the account email and plan at the top

screen2-a7.deciding_evidence: the initials avatar opened the account settings, as the avatar convention promises
